name: Vietnam
summary_text: Vietnam is broadly workable — described as "one of Asia's most tolerant countries toward sexual minorities." Same-sex conduct is not criminalised, and the Civil Code (2015, Article 37) was a landmark that recognised transgender people's right to change their legal gender. However, the implementing Gender Affirmation Law has been stalled for over eight years — the right exists on paper but not in practice. There is no anti-discrimination law covering gender identity. No trans-specific killing has been documented (unlike several neighbours), but conversion efforts (SOGICE) are documented, and healthcare discrimination is a significant barrier — trans people face stigma, lack of trans-competent providers, and "red tape" in accessing care. In September 2025, Ho Chi Minh City abruptly cancelled its flagship Pride march and five LGBTQ events, shocking activists (though Hanoi's Pride proceeded). For a visitor: no trans-specific border friction, bathrooms unrestricted, and no criminalisation. But Vietnam is a one-party authoritarian state where "rights lacked meaningful protection in both law and practice" (Amnesty), and the stalled LGR means no practical gender-marker change. The UN Development Programme is actively engaged on trans-rights strategies.

sources.title: Is Vietnam turning against LGBTQ+ rights?
sources.claim_summary: DW (Oct 2025): is Vietnam turning against LGBTQ+ rights? - Ho Chi Minh City abruptly cancelled its flagship Pride march and at least five other LGBTQ-themed events in late September, shocking activists; Hanoi events proceeded, suggesting a local decision; HRW's Patricia Gossman sees worrying signs of a clampdown possibly tied to internal power struggles.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying UNDP Vietnam blog explains why the gender-affirmation law matters - eight years and counting since the 2015 Civil Code amendment.

sources.title: Viet Nam | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex unions removed from the list of forbidden relationships; a law granting official recognition to trans people was supposed to be implemented in 2017 but obstacles persist to gender-affirming healthcare and marker changes; a draft law on the right to gender-affirming surgery is still under consideration (as of Feb 2026); LGBTIQ organisations operate openly but face government surveillance.

sources.title: Human rights in Viet Nam Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International Viet Nam report 2025: LGBTI people's rights lacked meaningful protection in both law and practice; vague Penal Code provisions used against dissent; concerns over ill-treatment of activists in prisons.

Lighthouse Vietnam study (Oct 2024): 'Exploring the lived experiences of conversion efforts (SOGICE) among LGBTIQ people in Vietnam' - documents experiences and forms of SOGICE in the Vietnamese context, with comprehensive data needs analysis.

sources.title: Voices from the Transgender Community: “Respect is the foundation for accessible healthcare.” | United Nations in Viet Nam
sources.claim_summary: UN Viet Nam story (Nov 2024): 'Voices from the transgender community: Respect is the foundation for accessible healthcare' - trans woman Tu Anh describes healthcare providers asking 'Are you male or female? Why do you look so different from your ID card?'; systemic barriers and stigma, doubly marginalising trans women from northern provinces and ethnic minorities.

sources.title: For Trans Vietnamese, Healthcare Providers Are Respectful, but Red Tape Still Hurts - Saigoneer
sources.claim_summary: Saigoneer (June 2023): for trans Vietnamese, healthcare providers are respectful, but red tape still hurts - the 2015 Civil Code amendment granted the right to apply for civil-status change and legal gender recognition, but implementation gaps persist.

sources.title: Responses to Information Requests - Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada
sources.claim_summary: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, Response to Information Request VNM201080.E (2022): 'Viet Nam: Treatment of individuals based on sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC) by society and authorities (2020–May 2022)', covering education, employment, housing, health care and state protection.

Viet Nam News (Nov 2018): 'Transgender law to be discussed by 2020' - the National Assembly was expected to discuss a draft law protecting the legal status and rights of transgender people (with or without surgery); ~300,000 trans Vietnamese face discrimination, and access to healthcare including hormonal therapy and psychological support is limited.
